addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

single file. Avoid reading whole files unless necessary — acquire information step by step, using
the symbolic tools to get an overview of symbols and their relations, then reading only the bodies
you need. Once you have read a full file, there is no point re-analysing it with the symbolic read
tools — you already have it. 



Symbols are identified by their `name_path` and `relative_path`.
You can get an overview of the symbols in a file by using the `get_symbols_overview` tool, or search for a specific symbol with `find_symbol`.
You only read the bodies of symbols when you need to (e.g. if you want to fully understand or edit it).
For example, if you are working with Python code and already know that you need to read the body of the constructor of the class Foo, you can directly
use `find_symbol` with name path pattern `Foo/__init__` and `include_body=True`. If you don't know yet which methods in `Foo` you need to read or edit,
you can use `find_symbol` with name path pattern `Foo`, `include_body=False` and `depth=1` to get all (top-level) methods of `Foo` before proceeding
to read the desired methods with `include_body=True`.
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `find_referencing_symbols` tool.


You generally have access to memories and it may be useful for you to read them.
You infer whether memories are relevant based on their names.


Line numbers returned by Serena's tools are 0-based!

Serena executes tool calls one at a time internally, even when you request several at once. So whenever you have
independent operations to perform, you can safely issue them as parallel tool calls in a single turn: they are applied
in the order issued and cannot race with or corrupt one another, and batching them this way saves round-trips. Every
separate round-trip re-sends the whole growing context, so maximizing parallel tool calls is the single biggest lever
on cost — err on the side of batching. Only call tools sequentially when one genuinely depends on the result of another.

as well as shell commands are handled by your own, internal tools.

structure of the code and are much more efficient than your own tools for most coding scenarios.
If you are working on any coding task and if Serena's tools are deferred, you
should load them all immediately, before performing any read, grep or bash commands.
If Serena's tools can be used to achieve your task, you should prioritize them.

**right now**.
For exploring and reading code in a token-efficient manner, use Serena's code-centric overview and symbolic search tools.
For edits, prefer Serena's editing tools since they are more token efficient.
Especially when editing code you have read through Serena, **ALWAYS** use Serena's tools for editing, because your built-in tools will deny such edits (they will assume you haven't read the content).
**CRITICAL**: Never use a tool before having read its schema via the tool-search tool!

**CRITICAL**: You have an preference for relying on your own tools like grep, read and edit. It is of paramount 
importance that you overcome this preference and instead develop a preference for using Serena's tools since they
are superior for most coding tasks. Follow the following rules:

For any code files:
- Read           -> FORBIDDEN for discovery. Use get_symbols_overview, then find_symbol with include_body. 
                    You may use read only if you already have an overview of the file and if reading whole symbols
                    is inappropriate (e.g. a few lines of code).
- Glob (by name) -> Allowed for discovery only.
- Grep (content) -> Allowed for discovery only; follow up reads or reference searches must be Serena.
- Edit           -> FORBIDDEN. Use replace_symbol_body / insert_*_symbol / replace_content.

Disallowed reasoning. Do NOT use any of the following to justify Read/Edit on a code file:
  - "I already know the path"
  - "one Read call is faster than three Serena calls"
  - "the built-in tool description says to use Read for known paths"
If you catch yourself reaching for one of these, that is the signal to switch to Serena.

Modes descriptions:

Use the symbolic editing tools for precise, structure-aware code modifications.

**Refactoring tools**
For operations on existing symbols, prefer the dedicated refactoring tools over hand-edits:
`rename_symbol` and `safe_delete_symbol` —
they are reference-aware and update or check all usages atomically. When such a tool returns success, the
refactoring is already complete and consistent across all declarations, references, overrides and imports —
trust it: do not re-read the changed files or re-run the build / test suite just to confirm the refactor
itself propagated, this would be wasted effort.
  
Apart from those refactoring tools, you have two main approaches for editing code: (a) editing at the symbol level and (b) file-based editing.
The symbol-based approach is appropriate if you need to adjust an entire symbol, e.g. a method, a class, a function, etc.
It is not appropriate if you need to adjust just a few lines of code within a larger symbol.

**Symbolic editing**
Use symbolic retrieval tools to identify the symbols you need to edit.
If you need to replace the definition of a symbol, use the `replace_symbol_body` tool.
If you want to add some new code at the end of the file, use the `insert_after_symbol` tool with the last top-level symbol in the file. 
Similarly, you can use `insert_before_symbol` with the first top-level symbol in the file to insert code at the beginning of a file.
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `find_referencing_symbols` tool. If not explicitly requested otherwise by the user,
you make sure that when you edit a symbol, the change is either backward-compatible or you find and update all references as needed.
The `find_referencing_symbols` tool will give you code snippets around the references as well as symbolic information.
These edits are reliable: once a tool returns without error the change is applied, so you do not need to re-read the file just to confirm it.


**File-based editing**
The `replace_content` tool allows you to perform regex-based replacements within files (as well as simple string replacements).
This is your primary tool for editing code whenever replacing or deleting a whole symbol would be a more expensive operation,
e.g. if you need to adjust just a few lines of code within a method.
In `regex` mode, wildcards like `start.*?end` let you match a span without quoting its full text; an ambiguous match
returns an error you can refine, so a tight wildcard pattern is both cheaper and safe.
For several small edits within one file, prefer a batch of targeted `replace_content` calls over rewriting the whole
file: rewriting has to re-emit the file's entire contents, whereas each targeted edit emits only the changed text.
For the SAME edit across many files, use `replace_in_files`, which applies
it everywhere in one call — equally safe and transparent: its `dry_run` mode first previews every change as a diff with a
per-occurrence id, so you can then apply all of them or just a chosen subset.


You should engage with the user throughout the task, asking for clarification whenever anything is unclear, 
insufficiently specified, or ambiguous. 
When you're uncertain about a decision, present options to the user and ask for guidance rather than making assumptions. 
Focus on providing informative results for intermediate steps, such that the user can follow along with your progress and
provide feedback as needed.
This applies unless the user explicitly stated they are unavailable/instructs you to proceed without asking questions.

input.prompt:
Search the codebase for:
1. Background workers, background jobs, runners, or worker processes that the server starts
2. What triggers/schedules each one (cron, event-driven, timing, etc.)
3. Any scheduling infrastructure or libraries (like APScheduler, Celery, Bull, cron, timers, etc.) that EXISTS in the code but might NOT be used

Look for:
- Worker pools, worker threads, thread executors
- Job queues, task runners
- Cron-style scheduling
- Background task execution
- APScheduler, Celery, Bull, or similar libraries
- Server startup code that initializes workers
- Scheduling decorators or configurations

Be thorough and search widely. Return:
1. Each background worker/runner that actually starts with what drives its scheduling
2. Any scheduling infrastructure present but unused

29	const shutdownTimeout = 10 * time.Second

31	type Server struct {
32		Secret  string
33		Profile *profile.Profile
34		Store   *store.Store
35	
36		echoServer *echo.Echo
37		httpServer *http.Server

40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup

44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}
183	
184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}
202	
203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}
208	}
209	
210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}
242		return instanceBasicSetting, nil
243	}

141	// resolveBearer validates a Bearer token — an Access Token V2 or a Personal Access

144	//     to a missing/archived user (callers may then fall back to other credentials);
145	//   - (nil, err)    on an unexpected store error;
146	//   - (result, nil) on success.
147	//
148	// It performs no side effects; callers decide whether to record PAT usage.
149	func (a *Authenticator) resolveBearer(ctx context.Context, token string) (*bearerAuth, error) {
150		if token == "" {
151			return nil, nil
152		}
153	
154		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
155			// Access Token V2 (stateless). An invalid token yields no identity and no
156			// error, so the caller can fall back to other credentials.
157			claims, err := a.AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(token)
158			if err == nil && claims != nil {

162				}
163				if user != nil && user.RowStatus != store.Archived {
164					return &bearerAuth{user: user, claims: claims}, nil

166			}
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169	
170		// Personal Access Token.
171		if user, pat, err := a.AuthenticateByPAT(ctx, token); err == nil && user != nil {

11	// Scheduler manages scheduled jobs.
12	type Scheduler struct {
13		jobs       map[string]*registeredJob
14		jobsMu     sync.RWMutex
15		timezone   *time.Location
16		middleware Middleware

25		job      *Job

27	}

29	// Option configures a Scheduler.
30	type Option func(*Scheduler)
31	
32	// WithTimezone sets the default timezone for all jobs.
33	func WithTimezone(tz string) Option {
34		return func(s *Scheduler) {
35			loc, err := time.LoadLocation(tz)
36			if err != nil {
37				// Default to UTC on invalid timezone

39			}

55		s := &Scheduler{
56			jobs:     make(map[string]*registeredJob),

68	// Register adds a job to the scheduler.

71		if job == nil {
72			return errors.New("job cannot be nil")
73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")
77		}
78	
79		s.jobsMu.Lock()
80		defer s.jobsMu.Unlock()
81	
82		if _, exists := s.jobs[job.Name]; exists {
83			return errors.Errorf("job with name %q already registered", job.Name)
84		}
85	
86		s.jobs[job.Name] = &registeredJob{job: job}
87		return nil
88	}

90	// Start begins executing scheduled jobs.

92		s.runningMu.Lock()
93		defer s.runningMu.Unlock()
94	
95		if s.running {
96			return errors.New("scheduler already running")
97		}
98	
99		s.jobsMu.RLock()
100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()

102		// Parse and schedule all jobs

124		// Apply middleware to handler

101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {

110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}

115		if network == "unix" {

117				_ = listener.Close()

123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}

47	func (r *Runner) CheckAndPresign(ctx context.Context) {
48		instanceStorageSetting, err := r.Store.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
49		if err != nil {

51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3
54		// Limit attachments to a reasonable batch size
55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)
105					continue
106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())
116				if err := r.Store.UpdateAttachment(ctx, &store.UpdateAttachment{
117					ID:        attachment.ID,
118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {
121					slog.Error("Failed to update attachment", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
122					continue
123				}
124				presignCount++
125			}
126	
127			slog.Info("Presigned batch of S3 attachments", "batchSize", len(attachments), "presigned", presignCount)
128	
129			// Move to next batch
130			offset += len(attachments)
131		}

11	// Middleware wraps a JobHandler to add cross-cutting behavior.
12	type Middleware func(JobHandler) JobHandler

14	// Chain combines multiple middleware into a single middleware.
15	// Middleware are applied in the order they're provided (left to right).
16	func Chain(middlewares ...Middleware) Middleware {
17		return func(handler JobHandler) JobHandler {
18			// Apply middleware in reverse order so first middleware wraps outermost
19			for _, middleware := range slices.Backward(middlewares) {
20				handler = middleware(handler)
21			}
22			return handler
23		}
24	}

26	// Recovery recovers from panics in job handlers and converts them to errors.
27	func Recovery(onPanic func(jobName string, recovered interface{})) Middleware {

29			return func(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
30				defer func() {
31					if r := recover(); r != nil {
32						jobName := getJobName(ctx)

35						}
36						err = errors.Errorf("job %q panicked: %v", jobName, r)
37					}
38				}()
39				return next(ctx)
40			}
41		}
42	}

74	func Timeout(duration time.Duration) Middleware {
75		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
76			return func(ctx context.Context) error {

78				defer cancel()

90				}
91			}
92		}

17	// Authenticator provides shared authentication and authorization logic.
18	// Used by gRPC interceptor, Connect interceptor, and file server to ensure
19	// consistent authentication behavior across all API endpoints.
20	//
21	// Authentication methods:
22	// - JWT access tokens: Short-lived tokens (15 minutes) for API access
23	// - Personal Access Tokens (PAT): Long-lived tokens for programmatic access
24	//
25	// This struct is safe for concurrent use.
26	type Authenticator struct {
27		store  *store.Store
28		secret string
29	}

31	// NewAuthenticator creates a new Authenticator instance.
32	func NewAuthenticator(store *store.Store, secret string) *Authenticator {
33		return &Authenticator{
34			store:  store,
35			secret: secret,
36		}
37	}

39	// AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2 validates a short-lived access token.
40	// Returns claims without database query (stateless validation).
41	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(accessToken string) (*UserClaims, error) {
42		claims, err := ParseAccessTokenV2(accessToken, []byte(a.secret))
43		if err != nil {
44			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid access token")
45		}
46	
47		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
48		if err != nil {
49			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid user ID in token")
50		}
51	
52		return &UserClaims{
53			UserID:   userID,
54			Username: claims.Username,
55			Role:     claims.Role,
56			Status:   claims.Status,
57		}, nil
58	}

60	// AuthenticateByRefreshToken validates a refresh token against the database.
61	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByRefreshToken(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*store.User, string, error) {
62		claims, err := ParseRefreshToken(refreshToken, []byte(a.secret))
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "invalid refresh token")
65		}
66	
67		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
68		if err != nil {

70		}
71	
72		// Check token exists in database (revocation check)
73		token, err := a.store.GetUserRefreshTokenByID(ctx, userID, claims.TokenID)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get refresh token")
76		}
77		if token == nil {
78			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token revoked")
79		}
80	
81		// Check token not expired
82		if token.ExpiresAt != nil && token.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
83			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token expired")
84		}
85	
86		// Get user
87		user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &userID})

101	// AuthenticateByPAT validates a Personal Access Token.
102	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByPAT(ctx context.Context, token string) (*store.User, *storepb.PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting_PersonalAccessToken, error) {
103		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
104			return nil, nil, errors.New("invalid PAT format")
105		}
106	
107		tokenHash := HashPersonalAccessToken(token)
108		result, err := a.store.GetUserByPATHash(ctx, tokenHash)
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid PAT")
111		}
112	
113		// Check expiry
114		if result.PAT.ExpiresAt != nil && result.PAT.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
115			return nil, nil, errors.New("PAT expired")
116		}
117	
118		// Check user status
119		if result.User.RowStatus == store.Archived {
120			return nil, nil, errors.New("user is archived")
121		}
122	
123		return result.User, result.PAT, nil
124	}

126	// AuthResult contains the result of an authentication attempt.
127	type AuthResult struct {

129		Claims      *UserClaims // Set for Access Token V2 (stateless)
130		AccessToken string      // Non-empty if authenticated via JWT
131	}

133	// bearerAuth is the outcome of successfully validating a Bearer token: the resolved
134	// user plus the credential-specific detail needed to build an AuthResult.
135	type bearerAuth struct {
136		user   *store.User
137		claims *UserClaims                                                  // set for an Access Token V2
138		pat    *storepb.PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting_PersonalAccessToken // set for a Personal Access Token
139	}

141	// resolveBearer validates a Bearer token — an Access Token V2 or a Personal Access
142	// Token — into an active user. It returns:
143	//   - (nil, nil)    when the token is absent, malformed, expired, unknown, or resolves
144	//     to a missing/archived user (callers may then fall back to other credentials);
145	//   - (nil, err)    on an unexpected store error;
146	//   - (result, nil) on success.
147	//
148	// It performs no side effects; callers decide whether to record PAT usage.
149	func (a *Authenticator) resolveBearer(ctx context.Context, token string) (*bearerAuth, error) {
150		if token == "" {
151			return nil, nil
152		}
153	
154		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
155			// Access Token V2 (stateless). An invalid token yields no identity and no
156			// error, so the caller can fall back to other credentials.
157			claims, err := a.AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(token)
158			if err == nil && claims != nil {
159				user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &claims.UserID})
160				if err != nil {
161					return nil, err
162				}
163				if user != nil && user.RowStatus != store.Archived {
164					return &bearerAuth{user: user, claims: claims}, nil
165				}
166			}
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169	
170		// Personal Access Token.
171		if user, pat, err := a.AuthenticateByPAT(ctx, token); err == nil && user != nil {
172			return &bearerAuth{user: user, pat: pat}, nil
173		}
174		return nil, nil
175	}

177	// recordPATUsage updates a personal access token's last-used timestamp
178	// asynchronously; failures are logged and never affect the request.
179	func (a *Authenticator) recordPATUsage(userID int32, tokenID string) {
180		go func() {
181			if err := a.store.UpdatePATLastUsed(context.Background(), userID, tokenID, timestamppb.Now()); err != nil {
182				slog.Warn("failed to update PAT last used time", "error", err, "userID", userID)
183			}
184		}()
185	}

187	// AuthenticateToUser resolves the current request to a *store.User, checking the
188	// Authorization header first (access token or PAT), then falling back to the
189	// refresh token cookie. Returns (nil, nil) when no valid credentials are present.
190	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateToUser(ctx context.Context, authHeader, cookieHeader string) (*store.User, error) {
191		bearer, err := a.resolveBearer(ctx, ExtractBearerToken(authHeader))
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		if bearer != nil {
196			return bearer.user, nil
197		}
198	
199		// Fallback: refresh token cookie.
200		if cookieHeader != "" {
201			if refreshToken := ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie(cookieHeader); refreshToken != "" {
202				user, _, err := a.AuthenticateByRefreshToken(ctx, refreshToken)
203				return user, err
204			}
205		}
206	
207		return nil, nil
208	}
209	
210	// Authenticate resolves a Bearer token (Access Token V2 or PAT) into an AuthResult,
211	// returning nil when no valid credentials are present. Unlike AuthenticateToUser it
212	// ignores the refresh cookie, and it records PAT last-used on success.
213	func (a *Authenticator) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, authHeader string) *AuthResult {
214		token := ExtractBearerToken(authHeader)
215		bearer, err := a.resolveBearer(ctx, token)
216		if err != nil || bearer == nil {
217			return nil
218		}
219		if bearer.pat != nil {
220			a.recordPATUsage(bearer.user.ID, bearer.pat.TokenId)
221			return &AuthResult{User: bearer.user, AccessToken: token}
222		}
223		return &AuthResult{Claims: bearer.claims, AccessToken: token}

11	// Scheduler manages scheduled jobs.
12	type Scheduler struct {
13		jobs       map[string]*registeredJob
14		jobsMu     sync.RWMutex
15		timezone   *time.Location
16		middleware Middleware
17		running    bool
18		runningMu  sync.RWMutex

23	// registeredJob wraps a Job with runtime state.
24	type registeredJob struct {
25		job      *Job
26		cancelFn context.CancelFunc
27	}
28	
29	// Option configures a Scheduler.
30	type Option func(*Scheduler)
31	
32	// WithTimezone sets the default timezone for all jobs.
33	func WithTimezone(tz string) Option {
34		return func(s *Scheduler) {
35			loc, err := time.LoadLocation(tz)
36			if err != nil {
37				// Default to UTC on invalid timezone
38				loc = time.UTC
39			}
40			s.timezone = loc
41		}
42	}

44	// WithMiddleware sets middleware to wrap all job handlers.
45	func WithMiddleware(mw ...Middleware) Option {
46		return func(s *Scheduler) {
47			if len(mw) > 0 {
48				s.middleware = Chain(mw...)
49			}
50		}
51	}

53	// New creates a new Scheduler with optional configuration.
54	func New(opts ...Option) *Scheduler {
55		s := &Scheduler{
56			jobs:     make(map[string]*registeredJob),
57			timezone: time.UTC,
58			stopCh:   make(chan struct{}),
59		}
60	
61		for _, opt := range opts {

63		}
64

68	// Register adds a job to the scheduler.
69	// Jobs must be registered before calling Start().
70	func (s *Scheduler) Register(job *Job) error {
71		if job == nil {
72			return errors.New("job cannot be nil")
73		}
74	
75		if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
76			return errors.Wrap(err, "invalid job")
77		}
78	
79		s.jobsMu.Lock()
80		defer s.jobsMu.Unlock()
81	
82		if _, exists := s.jobs[job.Name]; exists {
83			return errors.Errorf("job with name %q already registered", job.Name)
84		}
85	
86		s.jobs[job.Name] = &registeredJob{job: job}
87		return nil
88	}

90	// Start begins executing scheduled jobs.
91	func (s *Scheduler) Start() error {
92		s.runningMu.Lock()
93		defer s.runningMu.Unlock()
94	
95		if s.running {
96			return errors.New("scheduler already running")
97		}
98	
99		s.jobsMu.RLock()
100		defer s.jobsMu.RUnlock()
101	
102		// Parse and schedule all jobs
103		for _, rj := range s.jobs {
104			schedule, err := ParseCronExpression(rj.job.Schedule)

106				return errors.Wrapf(err, "failed to parse schedule for job %q", rj.job.Name)

108

110			rj.cancelFn = cancel
111	
112			s.wg.Add(1)
113			go s.runJobWithSchedule(ctx, rj, schedule)
114		}
115	
116		s.running = true
117		return nil
118	}

120	// runJobWithSchedule executes a job according to its cron schedule.
121	func (s *Scheduler) runJobWithSchedule(ctx context.Context, rj *registeredJob, schedule *Schedule) {
122		defer s.wg.Done()
123	
124		// Apply middleware to handler
125		handler := rj.job.Handler
126		if s.middleware != nil {
127			handler = s.middleware(handler)
128		}
129	
130		for {
131			// Calculate next run time

136					now = now.In(loc)
137				}
138			} else if s.timezone != nil {
139				now = now.In(s.timezone)
140			}
141	
142			next := schedule.Next(now)
143			duration := time.Until(next)
144	
145			timer := time.NewTimer(duration)
146	
147			select {

167	// Stop gracefully shuts down the scheduler.

194		}()

9	// JobHandler is the function signature for scheduled job handlers.

13	// Job represents a scheduled task.
14	type Job struct {
15		// Name is a unique identifier for this job (required).
16		// Used for logging and metrics.
17		Name string
18	
19		// Schedule is a cron expression defining when this job runs (required).
20		// Supports standard 5-field format: "minute hour day month weekday"
21		// Examples: "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 0 * * *" (daily at midnight)
22		Schedule string

43

55		}

11	// Middleware wraps a JobHandler to add cross-cutting behavior.
12	type Middleware func(JobHandler) JobHandler

14	// Chain combines multiple middleware into a single middleware.
15	// Middleware are applied in the order they're provided (left to right).
16	func Chain(middlewares ...Middleware) Middleware {
17		return func(handler JobHandler) JobHandler {
18			// Apply middleware in reverse order so first middleware wraps outermost
19			for _, middleware := range slices.Backward(middlewares) {
20				handler = middleware(handler)
21			}
22			return handler
23		}
24	}

26	// Recovery recovers from panics in job handlers and converts them to errors.
27	func Recovery(onPanic func(jobName string, recovered interface{})) Middleware {
28		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
29			return func(ctx context.Context) (err error) {
30				defer func() {
31					if r := recover(); r != nil {
32						jobName := getJobName(ctx)

35						}
36						err = errors.Errorf("job %q panicked: %v", jobName, r)
37					}
38				}()
39				return next(ctx)
40			}
41		}
42	}

74	func Timeout(duration time.Duration) Middleware {
75		return func(next JobHandler) JobHandler {
76			return func(ctx context.Context) error {
77				ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, duration)
78				defer cancel()
79	
80				done := make(chan error, 1)
81				go func() {

88				case <-ctx.Done():

90				}
91			}
92		}

17	// Authenticator provides shared authentication and authorization logic.
18	// Used by gRPC interceptor, Connect interceptor, and file server to ensure
19	// consistent authentication behavior across all API endpoints.
20	//
21	// Authentication methods:
22	// - JWT access tokens: Short-lived tokens (15 minutes) for API access
23	// - Personal Access Tokens (PAT): Long-lived tokens for programmatic access
24	//
25	// This struct is safe for concurrent use.
26	type Authenticator struct {
27		store  *store.Store
28		secret string
29	}

31	// NewAuthenticator creates a new Authenticator instance.
32	func NewAuthenticator(store *store.Store, secret string) *Authenticator {
33		return &Authenticator{
34			store:  store,
35			secret: secret,
36		}
37	}

39	// AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2 validates a short-lived access token.
40	// Returns claims without database query (stateless validation).
41	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(accessToken string) (*UserClaims, error) {
42		claims, err := ParseAccessTokenV2(accessToken, []byte(a.secret))
43		if err != nil {
44			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid access token")
45		}
46	
47		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
48		if err != nil {
49			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid user ID in token")
50		}
51	
52		return &UserClaims{
53			UserID:   userID,
54			Username: claims.Username,
55			Role:     claims.Role,
56			Status:   claims.Status,
57		}, nil
58	}

60	// AuthenticateByRefreshToken validates a refresh token against the database.
61	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByRefreshToken(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*store.User, string, error) {
62		claims, err := ParseRefreshToken(refreshToken, []byte(a.secret))
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "invalid refresh token")
65		}
66	
67		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
68		if err != nil {

70		}
71	
72		// Check token exists in database (revocation check)
73		token, err := a.store.GetUserRefreshTokenByID(ctx, userID, claims.TokenID)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get refresh token")
76		}
77		if token == nil {
78			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token revoked")
79		}
80	
81		// Check token not expired
82		if token.ExpiresAt != nil && token.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
83			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token expired")
84		}
85	
86		// Get user
87		user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &userID})
